newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian lev eases to 473-475 per dollar at close.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian lev eases to 473-475 per dollar at close.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev eased to 473-475 per dollar at the close of the interbank market on Wednesday from 463-465 in the morning after a large final client started bidding for foreign currency, dealers said.
"A big fuel importer sought relatively large dollar volumes in the afternoon and banks cautiously lowered supply and raised their asks (for the dollar)," a dealer said.
According to traders, that client's demand was not fully covered today and was expected to be carried over to Thursday and increase the pressure on the lev coming from the longer value date.
"The value date of tomorrow's spot deals is December 27 and a very strong pressure on the lev could be expected," another dealer said.
Markets will be closed in Bulgaria from Monday through Thursday for Christmas holidays.
The current large spread between interest rates of dollar- and lev-denominated deposits allows for a daily lev easing of some two levs per dollar, dealers said.
The central bank's main interest rate is now set at 15 percent monthly or 180 percent annually.

Just before dollar demand rose the lev had gained to 458-460 due to large foreign currency supply and low demand, and the central bank was seen buying small volumes at those levels to boost its foreign exchange reserves, dealers said.
"Dollar supply kept rising for a third day in a row until the early afternoon today due to profit-taking by banks and clients in anticipation of a further lev rise", a third dealer said.
The lev opened at 522-524 on Monday and advanced to its Wednesday's highs as low lev liquidity made banks and clients sell dollars amid light demand. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-876032
